header: IN THE HIGH COURT OF SINDH, KARACHI
Date Order with signature of Judge
M/s. Ghulam Rasool Mangi and Muhammad Naseem, advocates for the applicants alongwith the applicants.
Mr. Iqbal Kalhoro, Addl. Prosecutor General, Sindh for the State.

Since the above titled three criminal bail applications arise out of the same incident, which had occurred on 21.10.2008 at 0020 hours within the territorial jurisdiction of Police Station Saddar, Karachi, and has resulted in lodging of two F.I.Rs. No.255/2008 and 256/2008, one under Section 353/324/34, PPC and the other under Section 13-E of Arms Ordinance, I propose to dispose of these criminal bail applications by this common order.
2. Before I proceed to examine submissions of the learned counsel, it will be advantageous to reproduce hereunder the contents of main F.I.R. of the incident, which read thus:

“That tonight complainant S.H.O./PI Muhammad Iqbal Awan alongwith staff each HC Ishtiaq Ahmed 9538, PC Abdul Sattar 14030, DR/HC Khalid Hussain 1116, in police mobile Government was busy in patrolling in the area for prevention of crimes when spy information was received that some persons were conspiring regarding shifting of weapons and narcotics, waiting for transport, on receiving such information at 0300 hours reached at Abbasi Shaheed Road, empty plot near NIC Building, where sex persons were found, complainant party tried to encircled them, who seeing police party started firing upon is in order to kill us, in reply to the firing, names of the accused were illuminated by the spy informant each Farooq s/o Yakoub, Irfan s/o Farooq, Haroon s/o Yakoub, Rehman Gull s/o Sehar Gull, Naveed s/o Abdul Aziz, Mehrun Nisa wife of Abdul Aziz, who succeeded to escape from the place of incident, when one of the accused Farooq alias Farooqa left one TT Pistol 30 bore without magazine with three live bullets which were taken up by the HC Ishtiaq Ahmed 9538 during chasing, accused Rehman Gul s/o Sehar Gull while escaping thrown away one thella which was taken up by HC Khalid Hussain 1116, in which charras weighing one killo grams was found, so also accused Mst. Mehrun Nisa wife of Abdul Aziz while escaping thrown one thella which was taken up by PC Abdul Sattar 14030, in which charras one killo 20 grams was found, out of recovered charras and pistol 30 bore without number were taken into custody, offence of the above said accused fall under Sections 353, 324, 34, PPC, whereas offence of accused Mst. Mehrun Nisa wife of Abdul Aziz and Rehman Gull s/o Sehar Gull fall within the purview of Section 6/9-C of the Narcotic Act, whereas offence of accused Farooq alias Farooqa s/o Yakoub falls within the purview of Section 13-E of Arms Ordinance, hence offence under Sections 353, 324, 34, PPC is being incorporated, offence against accused Farooq alias Farooqa and Rehman Gull, Mehrun Nisa is being registered separately.”

3. According to Mr. Ghulam Rasool Mangi, learned counsel for the applicants, in a chain of false criminal cases, the applicants have been involved due to grudge and enmity with the police, as can be seen from as many as 13 F.I.Rs. against them, which have necessitated filing of 19 bail applications before the High Court, which are fixed for hearing today. Further submission of learned counsel is that according to prosecution story, incident of ineffective firing has taken place, whereafter recovery of unlicensed weapons has been shown from the place of occurrence with further allegations against the applicants that some of them have managed to make their escape good from the place of incident also leaving behind narcotic substance in the form of “charras”. His further submission is that the case of the applicants is of further enquiry, as evident from the contents of F.I.Rs. and possibility of their mala-fide involvement in the commission of crimes is also there, therefore, interim pre-arrest bail earlier granted to them vide orders dated 19.11.2008 and 04.12.2008 may be confirmed in the same terms.
4. Mr. Iqbal Kalhoro, learned Addl. Prosecutor General, Sindh for the State did not dispute this position.
body: 5. After careful examination of the contents of the two F.I.Rs. and the material placed on record, I am persuaded to agree with the submission of Mr. Ghulam Rasool Mangi, learned counsel for the applicants that, prima facie, this is a case of further enquiry against the applicants and their mala-fide involvement in the commission of crime also cannot be ruled out.
6. This being the position, interim pre-arrest bail allowed to the applicants vide orders dated 19.11.208 and 04.12.2008 is confirmed in the same terms.
